# On-demand searches

A search reads one term over the last `24h`, `7d` or `30d` (`range`, default 7d) WITHOUT creating a keyword: "what was said about globex this month?" when nobody tracks globex. Each platform that can search back in time is read once (bluesky, hackernews, github, stackoverflow, reddit with its comments, x, youtube, linkedin, tiktok, instagram, facebook; `platforms` narrows it; devto and news have no search and come back skipped), at most 25 results a platform, and every result is scored for relevance, sentiment and intents against the company profile. `kind` (`brand`, `competitor`, `topic`, the default) and `context` tell the classifier what the term is, as on a keyword.

Results stay APART from the mentions: no alert, digest, report or count sees them, and a search never creates a keyword. `alreadyInWorkspace` on a result says the post is already one of the user's mentions. When the user wants to keep listening, create a keyword (rules/keywords.md); a search is a one-off look.

It costs $0.008 per scored result (a result the classifier could not score is free), and the balance must cover the most it can cost (`maxCostCents`: 25 results for each platform read, $2.20 for all eleven) or the answer is `402 insufficient_balance`; a workspace that never topped up gets `402 funding_required` (send the user to Billing). At most 10 searches an hour per workspace (`429 rate_limited`). Tell the user the maximum before searching every platform.

`POST /v1/searches` answers at once with the search `queued`. Poll `GET /v1/searches/{id}` every 10 to 20 seconds until `status` is `done` (usually a minute or two) or `failed` (no platform could be read); each entry of `platforms` says its own `status` and, when skipped or failed, the `reason` (`credentials`, `budget`, `rate_limited`, `error`, `timeout`). Then `GET /v1/searches/{id}/results` (`minRelevance=40` for the relevant ones), newest first, paged with `nextCursor`. Summarize results like mentions: platform, author, sentiment and intents, one line, the URL. Searches are kept 30 days.

Base URL `https://api.mentio.dev`, `Authorization: Bearer $MENTIO_API_KEY` on every request, JSON in and out. The `mentio` CLI command for each endpoint is listed for when it is installed (rules/cli.md).

## Examples

```bash
# What was said about a competitor this month, on three platforms
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.mentio.dev/v1/searches" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MENTIO_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"term": "globex", "range": "30d", "kind": "competitor", "platforms": ["reddit", "hackernews", "linkedin"]}'

# Wait for it, then read the relevant results
curl -sS "https://api.mentio.dev/v1/searches/srch_..." -H "Authorization: Bearer $MENTIO_API_KEY"
curl -sS "https://api.mentio.dev/v1/searches/srch_.../results?minRelevance=40&limit=25" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MENTIO_API_KEY"
```

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | CLI | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/searches` | `mentio searches:list` | List searches |
| `POST` | `/v1/searches` | `mentio searches:create` | Start a search |
| `GET` | `/v1/searches/{id}` | `mentio searches:get` | Get a search |
| `GET` | `/v1/searches/{id}/results` | `mentio searches:results` | List a search's results |

### GET /v1/searches

**List searches.** The workspace's searches, newest first, kept for 30 days.

CLI: `mentio searches:list`

Query:

- `limit` (integer): Page size, 1 to 100.
- `cursor` (string): nextCursor from the previous page.

Returns: 200, a `LedgerList` (see Shapes below).

### POST /v1/searches

**Start a search.** Search a term over the last 24 hours, 7 or 30 days, without a keyword.

- Results are scored and kept apart from your mentions.
- $0.008 per scored result; the balance must cover `maxCostCents`.
- See [Search](/guides/search).

CLI: `mentio searches:create`

Body (JSON):

- `term` (string, required): The word or phrase to search, case-insensitive, matched as the phrase (written joined or as a hashtag counts). Quotes are not needed.
- `range` (string): one of `24h`, `7d`, `30d`. How far back the search reads, ending now: 24h, 7d or 30d. Instagram reads at most its last 7 days whatever the range.
- `platforms` (array of string): one of `bluesky`, `hackernews`, `github`, `stackoverflow`, `devto`, `reddit`, `x`, `youtube`, `news`, `linkedin`, `tiktok`, `instagram`, `facebook`. The platforms to read; omit for every platform that can search a term back in time (bluesky, hackernews, github, stackoverflow, reddit, x, youtube, linkedin, tiktok, instagram, facebook). devto and news have no search and are reported as skipped.
- `kind` (string): one of `brand`, `competitor`, `topic`. What the term is to you, as on a keyword: brand (your company or product), competitor, or topic (the default). The classifier judges relevance with it.
- `context` (string): A sentence the classifier reads for this search only, on top of the company profile: what the term means here, what to ignore.

Returns: 201, a `Search` (see Shapes below).

### GET /v1/searches/{id}

**Get a search.** Its status, each platform's progress and counts, and what it cost so far.

CLI: `mentio searches:get`

Path:

- `id` (string, required): Search id (srch_...).

Returns: 200, a `Search` (see Shapes below).

### GET /v1/searches/{id}/results

**List a search's results.** The posts the search found, newest first, with their verdicts.

A verdict is null while it waits; `alreadyInWorkspace` says the post is already one of your mentions. Readable while the search runs.

CLI: `mentio searches:results`

Path:

- `id` (string, required): Search id (srch_...).

Query:

- `limit` (integer): Page size, 1 to 100.
- `cursor` (string): nextCursor from the previous page.
- `minRelevance` (integer, nullable): Only results scored at least this relevant (0 to 100); unscored results are left out when set.

Returns: 200, a `LedgerList` (see Shapes below).

## Shapes

### LedgerList

- `data` (array of object, required): Ledger entries, newest first.
  - `id` (string, required): Ledger entry id (led_...).
  - `kind` (string, required): one of `signup_credit`, `topup`, `refund`, `debit_keyword_days`, `debit_mentions`, `debit_comments`, `debit_searches`, `adjustment`. signup_credit, topup, refund, debit_keyword_days, debit_mentions, debit_comments, debit_searches (on-demand search results) or adjustment.
  - `amountCents` (integer, required): Integer USD cents; credits positive, debits negative.
  - `day` (string, required, nullable): Debit rows: the last UTC day the row settled (YYYY-MM-DD).
  - `units` (integer, required, nullable): Debit rows: cumulative units (mentions or keyword-days) settled up to this row.
  - `note` (string, required, nullable): Free text on credits and adjustments.
  - `polarOrderId` (string, required, nullable): Top-ups and refunds: the Polar order.
  - `createdAt` (string, required): ISO 8601 timestamp, UTC.
- `nextCursor` (string, required, nullable): Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last.

### Search

- `id` (string, required): Search id (srch_...).
- `term` (string, required): The term searched, as typed.
- `range` (string, required): one of `24h`, `7d`, `30d`. How far back the search reads, ending now: 24h, 7d or 30d. Instagram reads at most its last 7 days whatever the range.
- `kind` (string, required): one of `brand`, `competitor`, `topic`. brand, competitor or topic: what the classifier was told the term is.
- `context` (string, required, nullable): The hint the classifier read, or null.
- `status` (string, required): one of `queued`, `running`, `done`, `failed`. queued: accepted, nothing read yet. running: platforms being read or results scored. done: every platform reported and every result scored. failed: no platform could be read.
- `from` (string, required): The start of the window read (the end is createdAt).
- `platforms` (array of object, required): One entry per platform asked for, in the order asked.
  - `platform` (string, required): one of `bluesky`, `hackernews`, `github`, `stackoverflow`, `devto`, `reddit`, `x`, `youtube`, `news`, `linkedin`, `tiktok`, `instagram`, `facebook`, `appstore`, `googleplay`, `trustpilot`, `googlemaps`, `rss`. Platform: bluesky, hackernews, github, stackoverflow, devto, reddit, x, youtube, news, linkedin, tiktok, instagram, facebook, appstore (App Store reviews), googleplay (Google Play reviews), trustpilot (Trustpilot reviews), googlemaps (Google reviews of a place), rss (RSS and Atom feeds a keyword reads).
  - `status` (string, required): one of `queued`, `running`, `done`, `skipped`, `failed`. queued: not read yet. running: being read or scored. done: read and scored. skipped: not read (see reason). failed: the read failed (see reason).
  - `reason` (string, required, nullable): one of `unsupported`, `credentials`, `budget`, `rate_limited`, `error`, `timeout`. Why a platform was skipped or failed: unsupported (no term search on it), credentials (not connected on this deployment), budget (its monthly vendor budget is spent), rate_limited, error, timeout. null otherwise.
  - `results` (integer, required): Results stored for this platform, at most 25.
  - `relevant` (integer, required): Of them, scored relevant (40 or more).
- `stats` (object, required): Counts across platforms.
  - `results` (integer, required): Results stored.
  - `scored` (integer, required): Results scored (the rest wait or failed).
  - `relevant` (integer, required): Results scored relevant (40 or more).
- `costCents` (integer, required): What the search has cost so far: $0.008 per scored result, rounded to the cent. A result the classifier could not score costs nothing.
- `maxCostCents` (integer, required): The most it can cost: 25 results for each platform read, at $0.008 each. The wallet had to cover it when the search started.
- `createdAt` (string, required): When the search was started.
- `completedAt` (string, required, nullable): When it reached done or failed; null while it runs.

### SearchResult

- `id` (string, required): Result id (sres_...).
- `searchId` (string, required): The search it belongs to (srch_...).
- `post` (object, required): The post: platform, text, link, publish time and engagement.
  - `platform` (string, required): one of `bluesky`, `hackernews`, `github`, `stackoverflow`, `devto`, `reddit`, `x`, `youtube`, `news`, `linkedin`, `tiktok`, `instagram`, `facebook`, `appstore`, `googleplay`, `trustpilot`, `googlemaps`, `rss`. Platform: bluesky, hackernews, github, stackoverflow, devto, reddit, x, youtube, news, linkedin, tiktok, instagram, facebook, appstore (App Store reviews), googleplay (Google Play reviews), trustpilot (Trustpilot reviews), googlemaps (Google reviews of a place), rss (RSS and Atom feeds a keyword reads).
  - `kind` (string, required): one of `post`, `comment`, `repository`. post: a top-level post. comment: answers a post or comment (Reddit, Hacker News or YouTube comments, X or Bluesky replies, Stack Overflow answers). repository: a GitHub repository event (see post.repository).
  - `url` (string, required): Permalink of the post.
  - `text` (string, required): Title and body, truncated to 8 KB at ingest.
  - `title` (string, required, nullable): The post's own title where the platform has one (a story, thread, issue, question, article, video or titled review). Null on X, Bluesky and LinkedIn, and for posts ingested before October 2026.
  - `imageUrl` (string, required, nullable): A preview image of the post, when the platform sent one with it: a YouTube thumbnail, a DEV cover, a news article's sharing image, a Bluesky link card or image. Null otherwise.
  - `subreddit` (string, required, nullable): The subreddit a Reddit post was written in, without the r/ (SaaS). Null on every other platform.
  - `flair` (string, required, nullable): A Reddit post's flair, when its subreddit uses them (Question, Show and Tell). Null otherwise.
  - `repository` (object, required, nullable): A GitHub repository event's facts, on a mention whose kind is repository; null on every other mention. The sentence is post.title.
    - `name` (string, required): The repository, owner/name.
    - `event` (string, required): one of `new`, `traction`, `stars`, `growth`, `top`. What happened:

- new: it was created.
- traction: under 30 days old, it reached 10 stars.
- stars: it passed a star milestone.
- growth: it gained stars fast in a week.
- top: among the most starred naming the keyword, from a look-back.
    - `stars` (integer, required): Its stars when the event was found.
    - `weeklyStars` (integer, required, nullable): Stars gained in the 7 days before the event; null when that week is not known yet.
  - `links` (array of string, required): Links the post carries, in the order written, at most 20. Empty for a post with none, and for posts ingested before September 2026.
  - `publishedAt` (string, required): When the post was published.
  - `engagement` (object, required, nullable): Counts as the platform reported them at ingest, usually minutes after posting; a missing count is null. Null as a whole when a platform reports none, or before September 2026. X carries all six.
    - `likes` (integer, required, nullable): Likes or upvotes when the post was ingested; null when the platform does not report them.
    - `reposts` (integer, required, nullable): Reposts or shares when ingested; null when not reported.
    - `replies` (integer, required, nullable): Replies or comments when ingested; null when not reported.
    - `quotes` (integer, required, nullable): Quotes when ingested; null when not reported.
    - `views` (integer, required, nullable): Views when ingested; null when not reported.
    - `bookmarks` (integer, required, nullable): Bookmarks or saves when ingested; null when not reported.
  - `replyTo` (object, required, nullable): The post or comment this one answers; null for top-level posts.
    - `author` (string, required, nullable): Parent post author as the platform names them.
    - `url` (string, required, nullable): Parent post URL.
    - `text` (string, required, nullable): Parent post text, when the platform gave it.
- `author` (object, required, nullable): Who posted it; null when the platform gave no author at all.
  - `id` (string, required, nullable): Person id (aut_...) for GET /v1/people/{id}; null when the account is not in the audience yet.
  - `name` (string, required, nullable): Display name as the platform reports it.
  - `handle` (string, required, nullable): Platform handle derived from the profile URL, formatted as the platform shows it (@name, u/name); null where the platform has none.
  - `url` (string, required, nullable): Profile URL.
  - `avatarUrl` (string, required, nullable): Profile picture; null where the platform has none.
  - `followers` (integer, required, nullable): Follower count as of their newest post; null where the platform has none.
  - `influence` (integer, required, nullable): How far their voice carries, 0 to 100 from followers on a log scale: round(20 * log10(followers + 1)), capped at 100 (1,000 followers is 60). Null when followers are unknown.
- `classification` (object, required, nullable): The verdict, judged against your company profile; null while the result waits for the classifier.
  - `relevance` (integer, required, nullable): 0 to 100; null only when classification failed.
  - `sentiment` (string, required, nullable): one of `positive`, `neutral`, `negative`. positive, neutral or negative; null when classification failed.
  - `intents` (array of string, required): Intent and topic tags:

- buy_intent, question, complaint, praise, comparison, bug_report, pricing, hiring, event, promotional.
- churn_intent: leaving or replacing the keyword.
- testimonial: a customer vouching for it from their own use.
- industry_insight: analysis or data about the field.
- launch: a product or feature launch announcement.
- feedback: a suggestion or request about it.
  - `automated` (boolean, required): The post reads as machine-made (a bot or app account, a scheduled or templated post, an AI-written summary). A label only: it stays in the feed, delivered and billed as usual. false while unjudged.
  - `language` (string, required, nullable): The language the post is written in, as an ISO 639-1 code (en, es, de); null when unknown, not one of the 20 the classifier names, or classified before languages were recorded.
  - `confidence` (number, required, nullable): How sure the classifier is of its relevance verdict, 0 to 1. null when the verdict came without one: the fallback model judged, or the row was scored before confidence was recorded.
  - `note` (string, required, nullable): One sentence from the classifier explaining the score.
  - `failed` (boolean, required): true when the model could not score this post; it is not billed.
- `relevant` (boolean, required): Scored at or above the relevance line (40).
- `alreadyInWorkspace` (boolean, required): The same post is already one of your mentions (a keyword of yours matched it).
- `createdAt` (string, required): When the search stored it.
